source_review.notes: Checked all 12 structured references against current Apache Iceberg, Avro, Parquet, Delta Lake, Hudi, Confluent, and Protocol Buffers specifications/documentation. Verified field identity, schema resolution, defaults, promotions, logical types, column mapping, widening, compatibility direction, and version-gating claims in their stated scopes; all final URLs returned HTTP 200.

evidence: Checked definitions for schema mapping Sigma, field identity/name/type/nullability/default/meaning, encoded domains, resolution, fleets, and retained history.
Checked every displayed compatibility, domain, resolution, and safety expression for defined symbols and balanced syntax.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation consistently separates writer/reader direction, field identity, value domains, retained versions, and semantic/operational safety.

evidence: Executed schema-identity-resolution and matched both schemas, four changes, old-row projection, compatibility directions, and retired-ID rejection.
Checked the long counter example: 4,000,000,000 exceeds signed 32-bit maximum 2,147,483,647, so old int readers are not safe.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All concrete values and executable results were independently recomputed; sample-fit claims are explicitly not generalized.

evidence: Verified backward and forward definitions quantify old/new writer domains into the opposite reader schemas.
Verified lossless widening requires old-domain inclusion and identity-preserving conversion.
Confirmed observed narrowing predicate over X does not imply universal old-domain compatibility and that total safety is a conjunction of independent layers.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Directional compatibility and data-profile validation are mathematically distinct throughout the chapter.

evidence: Reviewed missing versus null/default, required adds, retired-ID reuse, position/name binding, nested moves, enum/union changes, integer overflow, decimal scale, timestamp folds/gaps, leading zeros, and invalid Unicode/parsing.

Reviewed mixed historical schemas, old readers/writers, compactor/vacuum clients, automatic drift, catalog divergence, feature irreversibility, metadata-only rollback, privacy erasure, and physical cleanup.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Adversarial analysis covers silent semantic corruption as well as explicit decode failures and operational incompatibility.

evidence: Traced stable field identity through rename/reorder/drop/add and verified no retired ID is reused in the model.

Confirmed mixed-schema resolution, compatibility horizon, defaults, table metadata dependencies, fleet gating, migration, rollback, deprecation, and cleanup invariants across exposition, examples, and answers.
Verified semantic compatibility is never inferred from physical decoding alone.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter keeps serialization, file, table, fleet, data, semantics, operations, and governance checks independent and conjunctive.

evidence: Reviewed the seven-step identity-safe rename proof from stable ID preservation through ID-bound projection and reorder independence.
Checked that the drop/add countercase invalidates the preservation premise and is correctly excluded.
proof_review.notes: The proof is valid only under its stated end-to-end stable-field-ID assumptions.

evidence: The rename argument is explicitly labeled a proof sketch.
The following paragraph disclaims name/position-bound consumers and semantic compatibility.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No observed data profile, vendor feature, or type conversion is mislabeled as universal proof.

evidence: Format and product behaviors are attributed to dated primary specifications/documentation and remain explicitly scoped.
The executable disclaims implementation of the named serializers/table formats, nested types, and engine defaults.
Compatibility matrices distinguish specification-compatible, implementation-tested, semantically accepted, unsupported, and unknown evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Specification rules, teaching abstractions, empirical fleet tests, and semantic acceptance are clearly distinguished.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the chapter end to end. It builds evolution from writer/reader resolution and stable identity, then covers every major field/type/null/default/nested change, table dependencies, drift control, fleet compatibility, migration, rollback, and cleanup without conflating syntax with meaning.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed the evolution contract, compatibility matrix, historical data profiling, engine/tool inventory, feature fencing, canary/shadow/backfill process, consumer migration, rollback boundary, deprecation, privacy, and observability for implementability.

pedagogical_review.notes: Reviewed progression from compact definitions through directional mathematics, practical mechanisms, proof sketch, executable resolver, trade-offs, 24 misconceptions, ten examples, cross-program connections, and five distinct exercises with worked answers. Connections accurately bridge DE-063 to DE-065/066 and API-052.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
